sn5.3:0.3: The Discourse about Kisāgotamī Thus I have heard:
sn5.3:1.1: at one time the Fortunate One was dwelling near Sāvatthī at Anāthapiṇḍika’s grounds in Jeta’s Wood.
sn5.3:1.2: Then the nun Kisāgotamī, having dressed in the morning time, after picking up her bowl and robe, was entering Sāvatthī for alms.
sn5.3:1.3: After walking for alms in Sāvatthī, and returning from the alms-round after the meal, she approached the Blind Man’s Wood to pass the day,
sn5.3:1.4: and having entered Blind Man’s Wood, she sat down at the root of a certain tree to pass the day.
sn5.3:1.5: Then the Wicked Māra desiring to give rise to fear, terror, and horror in the nun Kisāgotamī, desiring to drive her out of concentration, approached the nun Kisāgotamī, and after approaching he addressed the nun Kisāgotamī with a verse:
sn5.3:2.1: “Why do you, like one with a dead son, sit solitary with a tearful face,
sn5.3:2.4: do you seek for a man?”
sn5.3:3.1: Then it occurred to the nun Kisāgotamī:
sn5.3:3.2: “Who is this, a human or a non-human, speaking this verse?”
sn5.3:3.3: Then it occurred to the nun Kisāgotamī:
sn5.3:3.4: “This is the Wicked Māra desiring to give rise to fear, terror, and horror in me, desiring to drive me out of concentration, who speaks this verse.”
sn5.3:4.1: Then the nun Kisāgotamī having understood: This is the Wicked Māra, replied with these verses to the Wicked Māra:
sn5.3:5.1: “I am at the end of dead sons,
sn5.3:5.3: I do not grieve, I do not cry, I am not afraid of you, friend.
sn5.3:7.1: Then the Wicked Māra (thought): “The nun Kisāgotamī knows me!” and pained and depressed he vanished right there.
